notes:
Summary: inbound from doc-search demo page (self-serve). Small legaltech startup building a client-facing contract search + summarization tool. Interested primarily in Redwood Hosted API for embeddings + reranking to power fast doc search. Early discovery; wants simple integration to Pinecone but open to Redwood guidance.

Activity timeline (recent):
- 2026-01-20: Form submitted via /docs-search demo (free tier). Captured basic use-case and sample dataset size (~120k docs, 600k pages).
- 2026-02-03: Intro email from Jordan (AE) with quickstart link. Developer replied with API questions.
- 2026-02-11: Discovery call (Fireflies ff_2026-02-11_oakmere_intro). Attendees: CTO (Emma Ruiz), Staff ML Eng (Devon Park), Jordan (AE), Maya (SE).
- 2026-02-12: Follow-up email with Pinecone integration checklist + sample curl.
- 2026-02-18: Clarifying thread about embedding dimensions and batching.

Key quotes / signal: "We need search rerank to feel instant — our users are lawyers, impatient. 95th pct under ~200ms would be ideal, 99th under 500ms." — CTO (paraphrase).

Use-case details / requirements (from call and follow-ups):
- Workload: document search for contracts + clause extraction; primary flow is embed query, vector similarity, then rerank with short-context LLM call.
- Dataset: ~120k docs, compressed to ~30M tokens; expect steady growth.
- Throughput targets: bursty queries during business hours, ~40 qps peak for similarity lookups; average qps ~6. Rerank calls should be minimal per query (top-8 -> rerank).
- Latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end for search+ranks ~300ms ideal, p99 500ms acceptable. Cost sensitivity: high — startup budget, wants estimate for hosted per-month cost and options to reduce by caching/batching.
- Model preferences: prefer open models for cost but will consider Redwood-hosted smaller LLMs for rerank. Interested in Redwood guidance on model/quantization tradeoffs.
- Embeddings questions: dimensionality (do Redwood embeddings match common vector DB dims 1536/1024?), batch vs streaming embeddings, max batch sizes, per-request rate limits, and whether Redwood returns raw vectors or a persistence integration is recommended.
- Vector DB integration: currently evaluating Pinecone; asks if Redwood has reference connector or recommended pipeline (i.e., generate embeddings via Hosted API -> push to Pinecone -> similarity search -> call Redwood generation for rerank). Wants example code.
- Reranking pattern: run similarity -> fetch top N -> rerank with 1-2 LLM calls. Wants to understand token cost for reranking and if Redwood supports structured outputs for rerank decisions.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support SSO for their staff (SAML) and need audit logs for admin actions.
- Data retention policy TBD; they want retention controls and the ability to purge embeddings tied to specific customer data.

Technical open questions (prioritized):
1) What are the exact embedding vector dims and do they align with Pinecone/Weaviate defaults?
2) Recommended batch size for embedding 5k-10k docs incremental ingestion without throttling?
3) Streaming support for rerank responses vs single-shot? Any latency tradeoffs?
4) SDK examples (Python/Node) for Hosted API -> Pinecone ingestion pipeline.
5) Cost estimate for expected workload (40 qps similarity + rerank top-8) on Hosted API free tier vs paid.

POC plan suggested by SE: 2-week technical POC (ingest 5k most-relevant docs, build similarity pipeline to Pinecone, instrument p95/p99 metrics, run 1k test queries with rerank profile). Success criteria: search recall >= 92% on sample eval set; p95 latency <= 350ms; monthly cost <= $8k.

Next steps / owner notes: Jordan to send quickstart + sample embeddings snippet (done 2026-02-12). Maya (SE) to prepare a compact Pinecone integration guide and approximate cost calc (action: Maya). Schedule POC kick-off call week of 2026-02-23 (pending budget approval).

Blockers: budget and internal legal (data retention/purge) — Emma to follow up with their counsel. Also need clarification from Redwood about embedding dims and ingestion rate limits before POC can start.

Internal notes (AE/SE): good inbound signal — product-led signup with early technical engagement. SMB profile but with realistic growth; likely conversion to pay within 1-3 months if POC success. Keep messaging focused on Hosted API ease-of-use, Pinecone connector examples, and cost-saving tips (prefix caching, smaller rerank models, batching).
